name: Haji
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: McDowell, Jonathan & Karl Anderbeck. 2020. The Malay lects of southern Sumatra. JSEALS Special Publication 7. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press. hdl:10524/52473
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress for any lect (a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/intonation/suprasegment: 0 relevant hits; 'accent' only in the lay sense). Haji appears for classification, lexicostatistics (60-63% PSC), high-vowel lowering before *r (§5.3, p. 73 region), the -kan suffix (§5.12.4.3) and as a 'bundled isogloss' case (§8.1).

sources.citation: Anderbeck, Karl. 2007. Haji: one language from twelve? A brief description of an interesting Malay dialect in South Sumatra. In Chong Shin, Karim Harun & Yabit Alas (eds.), Reflections in Southeast Asian seas: essays in honour of Professor James T. Collins, Book II, 51-91. Pontianak: STAIN Pontianak Press. (author's preprint, 45 pp.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The only first-hand linguistic description of Haji; sections 3.2-3.6 treat sound changes from PMP/Proto-Malayic (vowel lowering before *r, penultimate vowel neutralization, *h retention), Lampungic loans, a 400-item wordlist, sentence list and a folk story. a full-text search for stress/accent/suprasegment/intonation: 0 hits; wordlist carries no stress marks.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-183 (submitted by K. Anderbeck): split [mly]; create [hji] Haji etc.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; administrative request citing Anderbeck 2007 as the evidence for Haji's distinctness.

sources.citation: Ratnawaty, Latifah, Zainul Arifin Aliana, Muslim & Ahmad Bastari Suan. 2002. Struktur sastra lisan Aji. Jakarta: Pusat Bahasa. 176 pp. ISBN 979-685-259-4

sources.note: Nothing; oral-literature study. §2.2 'Bahasa Aji' (p. 11) gives only location and neighbours. p. 2 states that the only prior study, Satun et al. 1985 'Struktur bahasa Aji', describes 'fonologi, morfologi, dan sintaktis'. a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/fonologi/intonasi: 0 hits.

sources.note: The only known linguistic description of Haji with a phonology chapter (per Ratnawaty et al. 2002:2 and Anderbeck 2007:4); Pusat Bahasa 'Struktur bahasa X' reports normally contain a 'tekanan' (stress) paragraph.
